raw.retained_raw_text: {"schema_version":"chat_response_v1","response_type":"answer","answer_text":"The light-dependent reactions convert light energy into chemical energy stored in energy carriers, and these carriers move that energy to the Calvin cycle. The light-dependent reactions use light to temporarily store energy in energy carriers [ev_005] [ev_008]. Photosystems absorb light and use electron transport chains to convert energy into the chemical energy of ATP and NADPH [ev_002]. The energy carriers that move energy from the light-dependent reactions to the Calvin cycle are described as \"full\" because they bring energy [ev_001] [ev_005]. These energy-carrying molecules travel into the stroma, where the Calvin cycle reactions take place [ev_007]. The Calvin cycle then uses the energy in ATP and NADPH to convert molecules into G3P, which is used to build carbohydrate molecules [ev_010]. After the energy is released, the \"empty\" carriers return to the light-dependent reactions to obtain more energy [ev_001] [ev_005].
